purpose: The one environment in which the published A1/A3/A4 snapshots reproduce byte for byte. Canonical means publication reproducibility: it fixes what 'the same numbers' means for this release. It is not a claim about physical truth, field behaviour, or agreement with any external reference.

image.digest_provenance: resolved from the registry manifest and re-verified before each use; never transcribed from memory

comparison.inside_the_canonical_environment: exact byte identity of results/summary.json, checked with diff. No tolerance is permitted here.
comparison.outside_it: scripts/compare_case_outputs.py against docs/release/portability_envelope.json, plus each case's own acceptance criteria. Byte identity is neither required nor claimed.

how_fragile_this_is.measured: The bare ubuntu-24.04 runner carries glibc 2.39 and CPython 3.13.15 -- two versions away on both axes -- and produces byte-identical output to this container. CPython 3.11 and 3.12 on that runner do too. So the canonical bytes are the Linux x86_64 result rather than a property of one image.
how_fragile_this_is.why_pin_anyway: Because 'the canonical environment' has to mean one exact thing when it is used to publish, and a digest is the only way to say that. The pin is a definition, not a superstition.

what_this_is_not: not cross-platform bitwise reproducibility: macOS arm64 differs in the last significant figures and is not required to agree bit for bit
not external validation: nothing here is compared against data this project did not produce

rasterised_artefacts.what: site/src/generated/figures/*.png and *.svg and their published copies under site/public/data/figures/, plus manifest.json and index.json, which record their byte counts
rasterised_artefacts.environment: the ubuntu-24.04 GitHub runner with the Node version pinned in .github/workflows/ci.yml (NODE_VERSION)
rasterised_artefacts.why_separate: Rasterisation is done by the Node toolchain and depends on the platform's font stack, so it has a different canonical environment from the Python case snapshots. Two SVGs also differ: f06 by one coordinate at 1.1e-13 user units, and b1-04 likewise, because the geometry itself is computed in floating point and not only the rasterisation.
rasterised_artefacts.gate: the site-release job re-runs the canonical sequence and fails if any committed generated file changes; on drift it uploads what the runner produced
rasterised_artefacts.harvesting_procedure: When these drift, take the runner's output from the canonical-generated-dist-* artifact and rsync it over site/src/generated/ and site/public/data/. Verified reproducible: two separate hosted runs produced byte-identical PNGs, SVGs and manifest.
rasterised_artefacts.do_not_run_npm_build_afterwards: `npm run build` in site/ begins with `node scripts/render-figures.mjs`, so it re-renders every figure on the local machine and silently undoes a harvest. This cost two CI cycles: the harvested bytes were correct on disk and were overwritten before the commit. Verify a harvest with `npx astro build` and `npx playwright test` instead -- the Playwright webServer runs `npx astro build`, not `npm run build`, so the suite is safe. Confirm the bytes survived by hashing one PNG before and after.
rasterised_artefacts.manifest_couples_them: manifest.json records each PNG's byte count, so the rasters cannot be reverted independently of it. Harvest the whole generated tree together or not at all.
